correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and arbitrary compatible positive clade family H, clusters form laminar families. The cherry-contraction induction constructs a binary tree avoiding any prescribed laminar family of forbidden clades. Positive-hierarchy quotient localizes negative queries to unions of children of unique minimal positive nodes; independently refining them with avoidance realizes every labeling exactly when H∪S laminar. A binary tree has exactly n−2 nontrivial proper clusters; maximum extensions give VC=n−2−|H| and the all-positive path of an adaptive mistake tree gives Ldim upper bound. Nonbinary variant follows by containment and upper bound. Weighted hierarchy EGF plus Lagrange inversion yields singleton-free Stirling face counts. Finite verifier independently checks 3019 supports through n=6 and 241 conditional Ldim cases. No finite-to-infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The previously known unconditional exact VC and Littlestone dimensions n−2 for rooted binary and unrestricted trees are explicitly excluded from priority claims. Earlier same-class scalar result asserts neither a complete all-support shattering iff condition nor the sharp dimension for every compatible positive history nor the shattering-polynomial interpretation. New claim supplies nontrivial binary avoidance lemma and all conditional configurations; no inspected primary source asserts stronger coverage. Abstract hierarchy counting itself is classical, not claimed new. Residual historical risk persists under different terminology.
residual_risks: Specialized older work may describe binary clade query shattering via laminar antichains or hierarchy refinements under different terminology.

value.rationale: The entire shattering simplicial complex and exact positive-history online capacity are natural invariants of hierarchical phylogenetic membership testing. The arbitrary-negative-pattern avoidance lemma gives a structural characterization beyond known scalar dimensions; the conditional formula quantifies the exact drop in adaptive complexity from each independently confirmed clade; precise face coefficients give all support counts, not just the maximal cardinality. Abstract hierarchy counts and unconditional dimensions alone do not support this value claim.
